newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Siberian KrasAir to carry fewer passengers in '96.
newsitem.headline: Siberian KrasAir to carry fewer passengers in '96.

text.p: Russia's largest Siberian commercial airline, KrasAir, will carry fewer passengers this year, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
Vladimir Medvedev, KrasAir general director, told Reuters the company could lose seven percent of its passenger volume in 1996. The airline carried one million passengers in 1995.
KrasAir operates 70 passenger and cargo aircraft, many of them outdated. Medvedev said the company wanted to replace 20 planes.

"We plan to lease or to buy new Tupolev-204 jets," he said, declining to say how the company would pay for them. "We have lost many potential customers because of falling disposable incomes," Medvedev said.
He also said that the company, based in the Siberian city of Krasnoyarsk, had nearly ceased cargo activities.
"A few years ago, we made five daily cargo flights from Krasnoyarsk," he said. "But this is the number of flights we have done over the first eight months of this year."
KrasAir was born out the Siberian division of Aeroflot when the former Soviet monopoly devolved into a handful of smaller private airlines in 1992.
He also said KrasAir sought to add more U.S. destinations.
The company began regular flights from Krasnoyarsk to New York via Moscow last year, but Medvedev said these flights were currently not profitable.
KrasAir has licences to fly from Kranosyarsk to Miami, Los Angeles and San Francisco.
